title: At 17 months, first looks were longer when a toy failed to fall off an edge
summary: At 17 months, first looks were longer when a toy was pushed past an edge and did not fall than when it stayed supported.
body: The same Perez and Feigenson study showed a support event about six months later, at 17 months. A toy was pushed along a surface. In the expected outcome it stayed fully supported. In the surprising outcome it was pushed completely past the edge and did not fall. First looks were longer for the surprising outcome, about 2.61 seconds versus 1.69 seconds. Overall looking was only marginally longer, so this card states the first-look result. The paper was published in PNAS on 28 June 2021. It reports the tested group, not a rule for every toddler.

sources.title: Stable individual differences in infants' responses to violations of intuitive physics
sources.author: Jasmin Perez and Lisa Feigenson
sources.note: Peer-reviewed PNAS paper, 28 June 2021, open copy PMC8271639. Paraphrase of the 17-month support first-look result, and the marginal overall difference.
